title: Beyond the Nexus
now: The road beyond the river, and more of the island to explore.
The next forces of the road: The Drift, The Burden, The Rust and The Night Warden. Their paintings are taking shape; their battles and music come next.
The moment the Nexus forms, when the seven marks come together.
Light and atmosphere for every new place, until each one feels as good as the gate road at dusk.

ask.q: Where would you linger: the City, the Green, or Mill Landing?
What would make a one-button rhythm battle feel good to you?
ask.hint: A forgiving beat, a big musical moment, a story told in paintings—or something else?

ask.q: Real-life movement can earn Light, if you want it. Would you use that? What would make it worth it?
Did you play The First World? What would you love to see carry over?

releases.title: The controller stays with the duel
releases.summary: In The Current's duel, the controller no longer also acts on the world behind it.

items.t: Pressing B in the duel used to open the pause card of the road underneath, and A or the D-pad could nudge the hero there. While the duel is up, the controller now belongs to the duel alone.

releases.title: Playable on the web, up to The Current
releases.summary: A concept build of Beyond the Nexus now plays in the browser, from the Nexus to The Current.

items.t: The studio page has a Play button. The build is in development and ends where the road does, so expect rough edges.
The Nexus, the City and THE HOUSE, the open road, Sloth’s one-button rhythm fight, the River road, and The Current’s three-round gem duel.
Winning The Current wakes her and ends the concept with a calm card: back to the studio, or keep exploring the road. Each new battle will move the end of the road forward.
Both work on the web, as they do in the full build.

releases.title: The Current wakes, and the music gets real
releases.summary: A new kind of duel on the River road, and battle music played by an orchestra.

items.t: Talking to The Current on the River road now opens a three-round match-3 duel: painted gems on a see-through water board in a gold frame, and a few named moves like Signal Flare, Still Water and Break the Loop.
The arena warms from violet night to golden clear as you win, and her bar fills with gold Clarity as she wakes. Each round win plays a painted moment, from the Dragons to the Pearl’s release.
Losing a round only means being pulled under, and you try again. There is no game over, and the duel is easy by default.
Cards drift past on the water, dark when she scores, then flipping bright and floating away when you do.

The battle music is now built from recorded orchestra samples: strings, harp, celesta, horn, brass, a drum kit and a concert-hall reverb. It builds across the rounds, from a moody cello line to Atlas’s horn theme to a last stand.
Win, and The Current wakes and changes. The river changes with her, and the boats return.

releases.title: Sloth wakes, and the river finds its way home
releases.summary: Two bosses, a longer road, and a build made for the couch.

items.h: A walk all the way out
items.t: From the Nexus through the City, the lamps and the Green, Atlas can follow the gate road to Sloth, then take the new fork down to the river.
The battles have found their rhythm: one button, painted comic panels and a Dueling Dragons summon. Sloth wakes instead of dying, and the road opens.
A broken aqueduct, drifting boats and Tobin the miller, whose wheel has stopped turning. The Current, a river siren, waits on the water.
The Current’s battle brings The Pearl, a new finishing move. Afterward the water clears, the mill wheel turns and the boats row home.
Walk, talk and battle with a controller. The journey is now in the living-room TV build.

releases.title: The first quest, and a world beyond the walls
releases.summary: Not playable yet. Here’s what grew in the build this week.

items.t: The Lamps on the Gate Road: an elder of the City asks Atlas to relight the lanterns on the gate road, and the beacon burns brighter for it.
A valley of fields, a quiet pond with lilies and reeds, blossom trees, cottages and a glasshouse, with the City’s spires far off through the haze.
Heather and wind-bent trees under a dusk sky, lanterns and fireflies, and a stone bridge where Sloth lies sleeping.
A musician, doves, kids at play, a sweeper, people sitting in the sun and a cat, with warm light in every window.
Atlas and Ora against Sloth, the first force of the road. It’s rough, and it’s how we’re learning what the real battles should feel like.

releases.title: First scenes beyond the Nexus
releases.summary: The first scenes of the build, all in a hand-built diorama world.

items.t: The domed hall of seven gates, and “Atlas takes form”: the marks wake, light gathers on the dais, Atlas takes a body and Ora comes to his hand.
The crowd on the temple steps, seeing Atlas for the first time.
One City for everyone, with the old stone circle and the fire at its heart, markets and pools.
The trading hall has a door in the plaza.
A wet causeway at dusk, the glyph ring gate, and the mourning stone colossus.
